title: DeepSeek publishes first audited revenue in a STAR Market filing by H1 2027
body: DeepSeek is preparing a raise at roughly 500 billion yuan, about $74 billion, seeking as much as 50 billion yuan — its second round in two months, weeks after a June raise of about $7.4 billion at a post-money valuation near 450 billion yuan. Alongside it the company has opened early deliberations on listing on Shanghai's STAR Market, the exchange's board for technology issuers, with an internal target of completing a filing this year; terms and timetable are both unsettled, and a US listing is treated as impractical given Congressional scrutiny of Chinese AI firms. The June shareholder register is what turns this into a threshold rather than a headline: founder Liang Wenfeng committed 20 billion yuan personally, Tencent put in 10 billion and battery maker CATL 5 billion to become the largest external holders, and China's state AI investment fund holds the only outside board voting rights. DeepSeek ran for years on Liang's quantitative fund High-Flyer, and that self-funding is precisely what let it ship cheap open-weight models without answering to outside capital or a quarterly clock. Two raises inside two months and a filing target mean that arrangement is over. The prediction follows from what a listing costs rather than from what it raises. A STAR Market prospectus carries three years of audited financial statements, an itemized research-and-development expense line and a stated use of proceeds, so the first time DeepSeek files, its revenue, its research and compute spending, and the capital intensity behind its models all become matters of public record. That lands harder for DeepSeek than for a typical issuer, because its reputation rests on a training-cost claim no outsider has ever been able to check. By H1 2027, DeepSeek publishes an audited annual revenue figure and an R&D expense line in a Shanghai STAR Market listing document. The lab that argued frontier work could be done cheaply will have to prove it on the same disclosure schedule as everyone else.

reasoning.because: Second raise in two months at ~$74B, plus STAR Market deliberations and a 2026 filing target
reasoning.given: Self-funding via High-Flyer has ended; a STAR prospectus requires three years of audited accounts
reasoning.so_that: DeepSeek's revenue and R&D expense enter the public record, making its cheap-frontier cost claim auditable
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; a Shanghai STAR Market prospectus or listing filing from DeepSeek
reasoning.plain_language: DeepSeek used to fund itself and never showed its books. To list in Shanghai it must finally publish real, audited numbers.

summary: DeepSeek is raising at about 500 billion yuan, roughly $74 billion, weeks after a June round, and has opened deliberations on a Shanghai STAR Market listing with a 2026 filing target. A listing document would put audited revenue and R&D expense on the record for the first time by H1 2027.
